label.en: Chief Official of the Central Capital

sourceDate.text: 詔京兆康王子太安為後

label.en: Director of Masters of Writing and Grand Marshal

units.zh: 文成皇帝七男：孝元皇后生獻文皇帝。
units.en: Emperor Wencheng had seven sons: Empress Xiaoyuan bore Emperor Xianwen.
units.literal: Emperor Wencheng had seven sons: Empress Xiaoyuan bore Emperor Xianwen.

units.zh: 李夫人生安樂厲王長樂。
units.en: Lady Li bore Changle, Prince Li of Anle.
units.literal: Lady Li bore Changle, Prince Li of Anle.

units.zh: 曹夫人生廣川莊王略。
units.en: Lady Cao bore Lue, Prince Zhuang of Guangchuan.
units.literal: Lady Cao bore Lue, Prince Zhuang of Guangchuan.

units.zh: 沮渠夫人生齊郡順王簡。
units.en: Lady Juqu bore Jian, Prince Shun of Qi Commandery.
units.literal: Lady Juqu bore Jian, Prince Shun of Qi Commandery.

units.zh: 乙夫人生河間孝王若。
units.en: Lady Yi bore Ruo, Prince Xiao of Hejian.
units.literal: Lady Yi bore Ruo, Prince Xiao of Hejian.

units.zh: 悅夫人生安豐匡王猛。
units.en: Lady Yue bore Meng, Prince Kuang of Anfeng.
units.literal: Lady Yue bore Meng, Prince Kuang of Anfeng.

units.zh: 玄夫人生韓哀王安平，王早薨，無傳。
units.en: Lady Xuan bore Anping, Prince Ai of Han; the prince died young and has no biography.
units.literal: Lady Xuan bore Anping, Prince Ai of Han; the prince died young and has no biography.

units.zh: 安樂王長樂，皇興四年封建昌王，後改封安樂王。
units.en: Changle, Prince of Anle, was made Prince of Jianchang in Huangxing year 4 and later transferred to Anle.
units.literal: Prince of Anle Changle, in the fourth year of Huangxing was enfeoffed Prince of Changchang, later changed to Prince of Anle.

units.zh: 長樂性凝重，顯祖器愛之。
units.en: Changle was sober and steady in temperament; Xianzu prized and favored him.
units.literal: Changle was by nature grave and steady; Xianzu valued and loved him.

units.zh: 承明元年拜太尉，出為定州刺史。
units.en: In the first year of Chenming he became Grand Commandant and went out as Dingzhou inspector.
units.literal: In the first year of Chenming he was appointed Grand Commandant and sent out as Inspector of Ding Province.

units.zh: 鞭撻豪右，頓辱衣冠，多不奉法，為人所患。
units.en: He lashed powerful clans and shamed the gentry; many broke the law under him, and he was widely hated.
units.literal: He flogged powerful families and humiliated the gentry; many did not keep the law and were resented.

units.zh: 百姓詣闕訟其過。
units.en: Commoners went to the capital to accuse him of misconduct.
units.literal: The common people went to the capital to sue him for his faults.

units.zh: 高祖罰杖三十。
units.en: Gaozu had him beaten thirty strokes with the staff.
units.literal: Gaozu punished him with thirty strokes of the staff.

units.zh: 貪暴彌甚，以罪徵詣京師。
units.en: His greed and brutality only deepened, until crimes brought him summoned to the capital.
units.literal: His greed and violence grew worse; for crime he was summoned to the capital.

units.zh: 後與內行長乙肆虎謀為不軌，事發，賜死於家。
units.en: Later he plotted treason with Inner-Steward Chief Yi Sihu; when it was exposed he was ordered to take his own life at home.
units.literal: Later he and Inner-Steward Chief Yi Sihu plotted rebellion; when the affair broke out he was ordered to die at home.

units.zh: 葬以王禮，諡曰厲。
units.en: He was buried with princely honors and given the posthumous name Li, meaning Fierce.
units.literal: He was buried with princely rites; posthumous title Li.

units.zh: 子詮，字搜賢，襲。
units.en: His son Quan, styled Souxian, succeeded to the title.
units.literal: His son Quan, style Souxian, inherited.

units.zh: 世宗初，為涼州刺史。
units.en: Early in Shizong's reign he became Liangzhou inspector.
units.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was made Inspector of Liang Province.

units.zh: 在州貪穢，政以賄成。
units.en: In his province he was corrupt; office went to the highest bidder.
units.literal: In the province he was greedy and corrupt; government was accomplished by bribes.

units.zh: 後除定州刺史。
units.en: He was later transferred to the Dingzhou inspectorate.
units.literal: Later he was removed and made Inspector of Ding Province.

units.zh: 及京兆王愉之反，詐言國變。
units.en: When Prince Yu of Jingzhao rose in rebellion, Yu spread false word of a dynastic crisis.
units.literal: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled, Yu falsely reported that the realm was in turmoil.

units.zh: 在北州鎮，咸疑朝廷有釁，遣使觀詮動靜。
units.en: Northern border provinces suspected trouble at court and sent agents to watch Quan.
units.literal: The northern garrison provinces all suspected trouble at court and sent envoys to observe Quan's movements.

units.zh: 詮具以狀告，州鎮帖然。
units.en: Quan reported the facts in full, and the provinces and garrisons calmed.
units.literal: Quan reported the full situation; the provinces and garrisons were settled.

units.zh: 愉奔信都，詮與李平、高殖等四面攻燒，[3]愉突門而出。
units.en: Yu fled to Xindu; Quan, Li Ping, Gao Zhi, and others besieged him from four sides and set fires;[3] Yu broke through the gate and escaped.
units.literal: Yu fled to Xindu; Quan with Li Ping, Gao Zhi, and others attacked from four sides and set fires;[3] Yu burst through the gate and fled.

units.zh: 尋除侍中，兼以首告之功，除尚書左僕射。
units.en: Soon he was palace attendant; for being first to report the rebellion he was also made left vice director of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: Soon he was made Palace Attendant; for merit in being first to report, he was also made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 薨，諡曰武康。
units.en: He died and was posthumously titled Wukang.
units.literal: He died; posthumous title Wukang.

units.zh: 子鑒，字長文，襲。
units.en: His son Jian, styled Changwen, succeeded.
units.literal: His son Jian, style Changwen, inherited.

units.zh: 後除相州刺史、北討大都督，討葛榮。
units.en: He was later made Xiangzhou inspector and grand commander of the northern campaign against Ge Rong.
units.literal: Later he was made Inspector of Xiang Province and Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign to attack Ge Rong.

units.zh: 仍兼尚書右僕射、北道行臺、尚書令，與都督裴衍共救信都。
units.en: He still held the right vice directorship, the northern route mobile office, and the directorship of the Masters of Writing, and with Commissioner Pei Yan relieved Xindu.
units.literal: He still held concurrent office as Right Vice Director, Northern Route Mobile Office, and Director of the Masters of Writing; with Commissioner Pei Yan he jointly relieved Xindu.

units.zh: 鑒既庸才，諸弟粗暴，見天下多事，遂謀反，降附葛榮。
units.en: Jian was a mediocrity and his brothers violent; when the realm fell into chaos they plotted rebellion and went over to Ge Rong.
units.literal: Jian was a mediocrity; his younger brothers were violent and rough; seeing the realm in turmoil they plotted rebellion and surrendered to Ge Rong.

units.zh: 都督源子邕與裴衍合圍鑒，斬首傳洛，詔改其元氏。
units.en: Commissioner Yuan Ziyin and Pei Yan jointly besieged Jian; his head was sent to Luoyang, and an edict stripped the clan of the surname Yuan.
units.literal: Commissioner Yuan Ziyin with Pei Yan jointly besieged Jian; his head was sent to Luoyang; an edict changed their Yuan surname.

units.zh: 莊帝初，許復本族，又特復鑒王爵，贈司空。
units.en: At Emperor Zhuang's accession the clan was allowed to resume its original name; Jian's princely title was specially restored and he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign restoration of the original clan was permitted; Jian's princely title was specially restored and he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 鑒弟斌之，字子爽。
units.en: Jian's younger brother Binzhi, styled Zishuang.
units.literal: Jian's younger brother Binzhi, style Zishuang.

units.zh: 性險無行，及與鑒反，敗，遂奔葛榮。
units.en: Treacherous and without principle, he joined Jian's rebellion; when it failed he fled to Ge Rong.
units.literal: His nature was treacherous and without conduct; when he joined Jian in rebellion and was defeated, he fled to Ge Rong.

units.zh: 榮滅，得還。
units.en: After Ge Rong's fall he was able to return.
units.literal: When Ge Rong was destroyed he was able to return.

units.zh: 出帝時，封潁川郡王，委以腹心之任。
units.en: Under Emperor Chu he was made Prince of Yingchuan commandery and given the emperor's innermost trust.
units.literal: In the time of Emperor Chu he was enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan commandery and entrusted with duties at the emperor's bosom.

units.zh: 帝入關，斌之奔蕭衍，後還長安。
units.en: When the emperor entered the Pass, Binzhi fled to Xiao Yan; he later returned to Chang'an.
units.literal: When the emperor entered the Pass, Binzhi fled to Xiao Yan; later he returned to Chang'an.

units.zh: 廣川王略，延興二年封。
units.en: Lue, Prince of Guangchuan, received his fief in Yanxing year 2.
units.literal: Prince of Guangchuan Lue, in the second year of Yanxing was enfeoffed.

units.zh: 位中都大官，性明敏，鞫獄稱平。
units.en: He served as grand director of the inner palace; bright and keen by nature, he won a name for fairness in trials.
units.literal: He held office as Grand Director of the Inner Palace; his nature was bright and keen, and in judging cases he was called fair.

units.zh: 太和四年薨，諡曰莊。
units.en: He died in Taihe year 4 and was posthumously titled Zhuang.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he died; posthumous title Zhuang.

units.zh: 子諧，字仲和，襲。
units.en: His son Xie, styled Zhonghe, succeeded.
units.literal: His son Xie, style Zhonghe, inherited.

units.zh: 十九年薨。
units.en: He died in Taihe year 19.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year he died.

units.zh: 詔曰：「朕宗室多故，從弟諧喪逝，悲痛摧割，不能已已。
units.en: An edict read: "The imperial house has suffered too many losses; my cousin Xie is gone, and grief cuts so deep I cannot master it.
units.literal: An edict said: "My imperial clan has known many losses; my younger cousin Xie has passed away, and grief cuts me so I cannot stop.

units.zh: 古者，大臣之喪，有三臨之禮，此蓋三公已上。
units.en: In antiquity great ministers were mourned with three personal visits—a rite reserved for the Three Excellencies and above.
units.literal: In antiquity, for the mourning of great ministers there was the rite of three personal visits—this applied to those of the rank of the Three Excellencies and above.

units.zh: 至於卿司已下，故應。
units.en: Ministers and offices below them were expected to attend in due measure.
units.literal: As for ministers and offices below that, they should attend accordingly.

units.zh: 闕自漢已降，多無此禮。
units.en: Since Han times the rite has largely fallen away.
units.literal: Since Han and downward the rite has largely been absent.

units.zh: 朕欲遵古典，哀感從情，雖以尊降伏，私痛寧爽。
units.en: I mean to follow the ancient canon and let compassion follow feeling; though rank demands restraint, private pain will not ease.
units.literal: I wish to follow the ancient canon and let compassion follow feeling; though I lower myself by rank, private pain will not be eased.

units.zh: 欲令諸王有期親者為之三臨，大功之親者為之再臨，小功緦麻為之一臨。
units.en: I would have princes in the closest mourning circle pay three visits, those in the great-achievement circle two, and those in lesser or finest mourning one.
units.literal: I wish princes with kin in the period of mourning to make three visits, those of great-achievement kin to make two visits, and those of lesser-achievement and finest-mourning kin to make one visit.

units.zh: 廣川王於朕大功，必欲再臨。
units.en: Prince Guangchuan stands to me in the great-achievement circle; I shall certainly mourn him twice.
units.literal: The Prince of Guangchuan bears to me a great-achievement bond; I must certainly pay two visits.

units.zh: 再臨者，欲於大殮之日，親臨盡哀，成服之後，緦衰而弔。
units.en: By two visits I mean: on the day of the great encoffment to come in person and exhaust grief, and after the mourning garments are complete to return in finest hemp and offer condolence.
units.literal: The two visits mean: on the day of the great encoffment, to come in person and exhaust grief; after the mourning garments are complete, to go in finest hemp and offer condolence.

units.zh: 既殯之緦麻，理在無疑，大殮之臨，當否如何？
units.en: Condolence in finest hemp after encoffment is plainly required; but is a visit at the great encoffment itself fitting?
units.literal: For finest-mourning kin after the encoffment there is no doubt in principle; as for the visit at the great encoffment—is it fitting or not?

units.zh: 為須撫柩於始喪，為應盡哀於闔棺？
units.en: Should one comfort the bier at the first mourning, or exhaust grief only when the coffin is closed?
units.literal: Must one comfort the bier at the first mourning, or should one exhaust grief at the closing of the coffin?

units.zh: 早晚之宜，擇其厥中。」
units.en: Whether early or late is better—choose the mean."
units.literal: As to whether early or late is proper, choose the mean between them."

units.zh: 黃門侍郎崔光、宋弁，通直常侍劉芳，典命下大夫李元凱，中書侍郎高聰等議曰：[4]「三臨之事，乃自古禮，爰及漢魏，行之者稀。
units.en: Cui Guang and Song Bian of the Yellow Gate, Liu Fang, regular attendant of direct transmission, Li Yuankai, master of ceremonies lower grandee, Gao Cong, secretariat attendant, and others replied:[4] "Three visits are an ancient rite, yet from Han through Wei few have practiced it.
units.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Cui Guang, Song Bian, Regular Attendant of Direct Transmission Liu Fang, Master of Ceremonies Lower Grandee Li Yuankai, Secretariat Attendant Gao Cong, and others deliberated:[4] "The matter of three visits is indeed an ancient rite; even through Han and Wei it has rarely been practiced.

units.zh: 陛下至聖慈仁，方遵前軌，志必哀喪，慮同寧戚。
units.en: Your Majesty is supremely sagely and benevolent and means to follow the former track; your will is true mourning, your heart the same as one dwelling in the mourning hut.
units.literal: Your Majesty is supremely sagely and benevolent and is about to follow the former track; your will must mourn the dead and your thought is the same as dwelling in the mourning hut.

units.zh: 臣等以為若期親三臨，大功宜再。
units.en: We hold that if the closest kin pay three visits, great-achievement kin should pay two.
units.literal: We your subjects consider that if period kin make three visits, great-achievement kin should make two.

units.zh: 始喪之初，哀之至極，既以情降，宜從始喪。
units.en: At the beginning of mourning grief is at its height; since feeling has already bent rank, the first visit should fall at the beginning of mourning.
units.literal: At the beginning of first mourning grief is at its utmost; since feeling has already lowered rank, one should follow the beginning of mourning.

units.zh: 大殮之臨，伏如聖旨。」
units.en: As for the visit at the great encoffment, we bow to Your Majesty's intent."
units.literal: As for the visit at the great encoffment, we bow to the sagely edict.

units.zh: 詔曰：「魏晉已來，親臨多闕，至於戚臣，必於東堂哭之。
units.en: An edict said: "Since Wei and Jin, emperors have rarely mourned in person; for ministerial kin they wept in the Eastern Hall instead.
units.literal: An edict said: "Since Wei and Jin, personal visits have largely been wanting; for kin among ministers one necessarily wept in the Eastern Hall.

units.zh: 頃大司馬、安定王薨，朕既臨之後，復更受慰於東堂，今日之事，應更哭否？」
units.en: When the Grand Marshal, Prince of Anding, died I visited him in person and still received condolences in the Eastern Hall; for today's rite, should I weep there again?"
units.literal: Recently when Grand Marshal, Prince of Anding, died, after I had already visited him I again received condolences in the Eastern Hall; for today's affair, should I weep again?

units.zh: 光等議曰：「東堂之哭，蓋以不臨之故。
units.en: Guang and the others replied: "The Eastern Hall weeping existed because the emperor did not visit in person.
units.literal: Guang and the others deliberated: "Weeping in the Eastern Hall was because one did not visit in person.

units.zh: 今陛下躬親撫視，羣臣從駕，臣等參議，以為不宜復哭。」
units.en: Now Your Majesty will comfort the bier in person and the ministers will follow your carriage—we hold there should be no second weeping."
units.literal: Now Your Majesty in person comforts and views; the ministers follow the imperial carriage—we your subjects jointly consider that one should not weep again.

units.zh: 詔曰：「若大司馬戚尊位重，必哭於東堂，而廣川既是諸王之子，又年位尚幼，卿等議之，朕無異焉。」
units.en: An edict said: "For the Grand Marshal, kin of the highest rank, the Eastern Hall is required; but Guangchuan is a prince's son and still young in years and station—deliberate as you see fit; I raise no objection."
units.literal: An edict said: "If the Grand Marshal is kin of weighty rank and position, one must weep in the Eastern Hall; yet Guangchuan is both a prince's son and still young in years and rank—you may deliberate as you will; I have no objection.

units.zh: 諧將大殮，高祖素服深衣哭之，入室，哀慟，撫尸而出。
units.en: On the eve of Xie's great encoffment Gaozu came in plain white and deep mourning, wept, entered the chamber, was overcome, comforted the corpse, and withdrew.
units.literal: When Xie was about to undergo the great encoffment, Gaozu in plain white garments and deep mourning robes wept for him, entered the chamber, was stricken with grief, comforted the corpse, and went out.

units.zh: 有司奏，廣川王妃薨於代京，未審以新尊從於卑舊，為宜卑舊來就新尊。
units.en: The relevant office reported: the Princess of Guangchuan died in the Dai capital; it was unclear whether the newly honored dead should follow the humbler old, or the humbler old should be brought to the newly honored.
units.literal: The relevant office memorialized: the Princess of Guangchuan died in the capital of Dai; it is unclear whether the newly honored should follow the humbler old, or the humbler old should come to the newly honored.

units.zh: 詔曰：「遷洛之人，自茲厥後，悉可歸骸邙嶺，皆不得就塋恒代。
units.en: An edict said: "For families who moved to Luoyang, from now on all may rest their bones on Mount Mang; none may bury in the old Dai tombs.
units.literal: An edict said: "For those who moved to Luoyang, from this time onward all may return their bones to Mount Mang; none may bury at the old tombs in Dai.

units.zh: 其有夫先葬在北，婦今喪在南，婦人從夫，宜還代葬；
units.en: If the husband was buried first in the north and the wife dies in the south, the wife follows the husband and should return to Dai for burial;
units.literal: Where the husband was first buried in the north and the wife now dies in the south, the woman follows the husband and should be returned for burial in Dai;

units.zh: 若欲移父就母，亦得任之。
units.en: if one wishes to move the father's grave to the mother's side, that may also be done.
units.literal: if one wishes to move the father's grave to join the mother, that too may be done at will.

units.zh: 其有妻墳於恒代，夫死於洛，不得以尊就卑；
units.en: If the wife's tomb lies in Dai and the husband dies in Luoyang, rank may not draw the lofty down to the humble;
units.literal: Where the wife's tomb is in Dai and the husband dies in Luo, one may not let rank draw the lofty to the humble;

units.zh: 欲移母就父，宜亦從之；
units.en: if one wishes to move the mother to the father, that should be allowed;
units.literal: if one wishes to move the mother to join the father, that should also be followed;

units.zh: 若異葬亦從之。
units.en: separate burial may also be chosen.
units.literal: if separate burial is desired, that too may be followed.

units.zh: 若不在葬限，身在代喪，葬之彼此，皆得任之。
units.en: If the case falls outside these limits and the mourner is in Dai, burial on either side is at choice.
units.literal: If outside the burial limits, while the body lies in mourning in Dai, burial on either side may be done at will.

units.zh: 其戶屬恒燕，身官京洛，去留之宜，亦從所擇。
units.en: Where registers remain in Heng and Yan but office and person are in Jing and Luo, staying or leaving is likewise at choice.
units.literal: Where household registers belong to Heng and Yan but office and person are in Jing and Luo, as to staying or leaving, that too follows choice.

units.zh: 其屬諸州者，各得任意。」
units.en: Those attached to other provinces may each decide for themselves."
units.literal: Those attached to other provinces may each do as they wish.

units.zh: 詔贈諧武衞將軍，諡曰剛。
units.en: An edict posthumously made Xie General of Martial Guard and gave him the posthumous name Gang.
units.literal: An edict posthumously made Xie General of Martial Guard; posthumous title Gang.

units.zh: 及葬，高祖親臨送之。
units.en: At the burial Gaozu attended in person to see him off.
units.literal: At the burial Gaozu in person attended and saw him off.

units.zh: 子靈道，襲。
units.en: His son Lingdao succeeded.
units.literal: His son Lingdao inherited.

units.zh: 卒，諡悼王。
units.en: He died and was posthumously titled Prince Dao.
units.literal: He died; posthumous title Prince Dao.

units.zh: 齊郡王簡，字叔亮。
units.en: Jian, Prince of Qi Commandery, was styled Shuliang.
units.literal: Jian, Prince of Qi Commandery, was styled Shuliang.

units.zh: 太和五年封，位中都大官。
units.en: He was enfeoffed in Taihe year 5 and served as Chief Official of the Central Capital.
units.literal: He was enfeoffed in Taihe year 5 and held office as Chief Official of the Central Capital.

units.zh: 簡母，沮渠牧犍女也。
units.en: Jian's mother was a daughter of Juqu Mujian.
units.literal: Jian's mother was a daughter of Juqu Mujian.

units.zh: 簡性貌特類外祖。
units.en: In temperament and looks, Jian closely resembled his maternal grandfather.
units.literal: In nature and appearance, Jian especially resembled his maternal grandfather.

units.zh: 後為內都大官。
units.en: Later he became Chief Official of the Inner Capital.
units.literal: Later he became Chief Official of the Inner Capital.

units.zh: 高祖嘗與簡俱朝文明太后於皇信堂，簡居帝之右，行家人禮。
units.en: Gaozu once paid court to Empress Dowager Wenming with Jian at Huangxin Hall. Jian sat to the emperor's right, and they observed family rites.
units.literal: Gaozu once attended on Empress Dowager Wenming with Jian at Huangxin Hall; Jian occupied the emperor's right side, and they observed the rites of family members.

units.zh: 遷太保。
units.en: He was promoted to Grand Protector.
units.literal: He was promoted to Grand Protector.

units.zh: 高祖仁孝，以諸父零落，存者唯簡。
units.en: Gaozu was benevolent and filial; his uncles had died off, and only Jian remained.
units.literal: Gaozu was benevolent and filial; his uncles had fallen away, and only Jian remained alive.

units.zh: 每見，立以待之，俟坐，致敬問起居，停簡拜伏。
units.en: Whenever he saw Jian, he stood to wait for him; once Jian was seated, Gaozu respectfully asked after his health and prevented him from bowing prostrate.
units.literal: Whenever he saw Jian, he stood waiting for him; after Jian was seated, he showed respect, asked after his health, and stopped Jian from bowing prostrate.

units.zh: 簡性好酒，不能理公私之事。
units.en: Jian loved wine by nature and could not manage public or private affairs.
units.literal: Jian loved wine by nature and could not manage public or private affairs.

units.zh: 妻常氏，燕郡公常喜女也，文明太后以賜簡。
units.en: His wife, Lady Chang, was a daughter of Chang Xi, Duke of Yan Commandery, and Empress Dowager Wenming gave her to Jian.
units.literal: His wife, Lady Chang, was a daughter of Chang Xi, Duke of Yan Commandery, and Empress Dowager Wenming bestowed her on Jian.

units.zh: 性幹綜家事，頗節斷簡酒，乃至盜竊，求乞婢侍，卒不能禁。
units.en: She was naturally capable in managing household affairs and tried hard to limit Jian's drinking; he even stole and begged wine from maidservants and attendants, and in the end she could not stop him.
units.literal: By nature she was capable at managing household affairs and rather sharply restricted Jian's wine; he went so far as to steal it and beg maidservants and attendants for it, but in the end she could not stop him.

units.zh: 二十三年薨。
units.en: He died in the twenty-third year.
units.literal: He died in the twenty-third year.

units.zh: 時高祖不豫，詔曰：「叔父薨背，痛慕摧絕，不自勝任，但虛頓床枕，未堪奉赴，當力疾發哀。」
units.en: Gaozu was ill at the time and issued an edict: "My uncle has passed away; grief and longing crush me beyond endurance. I am weak and confined to bed, and cannot yet attend in person, but I will force myself through illness to express my mourning."
units.literal: At the time Gaozu was unwell. He issued an edict: "My uncle has died and departed; grief and longing crush me beyond what I can bear. But I am weak and prostrate on bed and pillow and cannot yet go to attend in person. I shall force myself through illness to send forth mourning."

units.zh: 諡曰靈王。
units.en: He was posthumously named Prince Ling.
units.literal: He was posthumously named Prince Ling.

units.zh: 世宗時，改諡曰順。
units.en: In Shizong's time, the posthumous name was changed to Shun.
units.literal: In Shizong's time, the posthumous name was changed to Shun.

units.zh: 子祐，字伯授，襲。
units.en: His son You, styled Boshou, succeeded him.
units.literal: His son You, styled Boshou, succeeded him.

units.zh: 母常氏，高祖以納不以禮，不許其為妃。
units.en: Because his mother, Lady Chang, had not been taken as consort according to proper ritual, Gaozu did not permit her to be made princess.
units.literal: His mother, Lady Chang, had been taken by Gaozu in a manner that did not conform to ritual, so he did not permit her to become the princess.

units.zh: 世宗以母從子貴，詔特拜為齊國太妃。
units.en: Shizong held that a mother follows the rank of her son and issued an edict specially appointing her Grand Princess Dowager of Qi.
units.literal: Shizong, on the grounds that a mother follows the rank of her son, issued an edict specially appointing her Grand Princess Dowager of Qi.

units.zh: 祐位涇州刺史。
units.en: You served as Inspector of Jingzhou.
units.literal: You held office as Inspector of Jingzhou.

units.zh: 薨，諡曰敬。
units.en: When he died, he was posthumously named Jing.
units.literal: When he died, he was posthumously named Jing.

units.zh: 河間王若，字叔儒。
units.en: Ruo, Prince of Hejian, was styled Shuru.
units.literal: Ruo, Prince of Hejian, was styled Shuru.

units.zh: 年十六，未封而薨，追封河間，諡曰孝。
units.en: He died at sixteen before receiving a fief; he was posthumously made Prince of Hejian and given the posthumous name Xiao.
units.literal: At age sixteen he died before being enfeoffed; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Hejian and given the posthumous name Xiao.

units.zh: 詔京兆康王子太安為後。
units.en: An edict appointed Taian, son of Prince Kang of Jingzhao, as his heir.
units.literal: An edict made Taian, son of Prince Kang of Jingzhao, his heir.

units.zh: 太安於若為從弟，非相後之義，廢之，以齊郡王子琛繼。
units.en: Taian was Ruo's younger cousin, which did not accord with the principles of succession, so he was removed and Chen, son of the Prince of Qi Commandery, succeeded instead.
units.literal: Taian was Ruo's younger cousin, which was not the principle for making one heir to another, so he was removed and Chen, son of the Prince of Qi Commandery, was made successor.

units.zh: 琛字曇寶，幼而敏慧，高祖愛之。
units.en: Chen, styled Tanbao, was clever even as a child; Gaozu doted on him.
units.literal: Chen, style Tanbao, was clever and quick as a child; Gaozu loved him.

units.zh: 世宗時，拜定州刺史。
units.en: Under Shizong he became Dingzhou inspector.
units.literal: In Shizong's time he was appointed Inspector of Ding Province.

units.zh: 琛妃，世宗舅女，高皇后妹。
units.en: Chen's consort was Shizong's niece by marriage, the younger sister of Empress Gao.
units.literal: Chen's consort was Shizong's maternal niece, younger sister of Empress Gao.

units.zh: 琛憑恃內外，多所受納，貪惏之極。
units.en: Chen leaned on court and family ties and took endless bribes; his greed had no bottom.
units.literal: Chen relied on inside and outside connections and received many bribes; his greed knew no limit.

units.zh: 及還朝，靈太后詔曰：「琛在定州，惟不將中山宮來，自餘無所不致，何可更復敍用。」
units.en: On his return Empress Dowager Ling issued an edict: "In Dingzhou Chen took everything but the Zhongshan Palace itself—how can he be used again?"
units.literal: When he returned to court, Empress Dowager Ling issued an edict: "At Dingzhou Chen failed only to carry off the Zhongshan Palace; otherwise there was nothing he would not seize—how can he be employed again?"

units.zh: 由是遂廢于家。
units.en: He was thereupon dismissed and kept at home.
units.literal: Thereupon he was dismissed and kept at home.

units.zh: 琛以肅宗始學，獻金字孝經。
units.en: When Suzong first took up his studies, Chen presented a gilt-letter Classic of Filial Piety.
units.literal: When Suzong first began his studies, Chen presented a gilt-letter Classic of Filial Piety.

units.zh: 又無方自達，乃與劉騰為養息，賂騰金寶巨萬計。
units.en: With no other path forward he became Liu Teng's adopted son and paid him bribes in gold and jewels beyond counting.
units.literal: Having no other way to advance, he became Liu Teng's adopted son and bribed Teng with gold and jewels numbering in the tens of thousands.

units.zh: 騰屢為之言，乃得兼都官尚書，出為秦州刺史。
units.en: Teng spoke for him again and again until he won the directorship of the Court for the Imperial Clan and went out as Qinzhou inspector.
units.literal: Teng repeatedly spoke for him; he then obtained concurrent office as Director of the Court for the Imperial Clan and was sent out as Inspector of Qin Province.

units.zh: 在州聚斂，百姓吁嗟。
units.en: In his province he amassed wealth while the people groaned.
units.literal: In the province he amassed wealth; the common people groaned.

units.zh: 屬東益、南秦二州氐反，詔琛為行臺，仍充都督，還攝州事。
units.en: When the Di of Eastern Yi and Southern Qin rebelled, an edict named him to a mobile office and kept him as commissioner while he resumed the provincial post.
units.literal: When the Di of Eastern Yi and Southern Qin rebelled, an edict made Chen Mobile Office and still charged him as Commissioner, returning him to oversee the province.

units.zh: 琛性貪暴，既總軍省，求欲無厭，百姓患害，有甚狼虎。
units.en: Greedy and brutal by nature, he now held army and province together and took without end; the people suffered worse than from wolves.
units.literal: Chen was by nature greedy and violent; holding both army and province he sought without end; the people suffered harm worse than from wolves and tigers.

units.zh: 進討氐羌，大被摧破，士卒死者千數，率眾走還。
units.en: He marched against the Di and Qiang and was shattered; a thousand soldiers died and he fled with the remnant.
units.literal: Advancing to attack the Di and Qiang, he suffered great defeat; a thousand soldiers died; he led the host in flight back.

units.zh: 內恃劉騰，無所畏憚，為中尉糾彈，會赦，除名為民。
units.en: Backed by Liu Teng within, he feared nothing until the chief commandant impeached him; an amnesty spared his life but he was stripped of rank and made a commoner.
units.literal: Relying within on Liu Teng, he feared nothing; the chief commandant impeached him; an amnesty came and he was stripped of name and made a commoner.

units.zh: 尋復王爵，後討鮮于脩禮，敗，免官爵。
units.en: His princely title was soon restored; later, campaigning against Xianyu Xiuli, he was defeated and lost office and title.
units.literal: Soon his princely title was restored; later in campaigning against Xianyu Xiuli he was defeated and stripped of office and title.

units.zh: 後討汾晉胡、蜀，卒於軍，追復王爵。
units.en: Later, campaigning against the Hu of Fen and Jin and the Shu, he died on campaign; his princely title was posthumously restored.
units.literal: Later in campaigning against the Hu of Fen and Jin and the Shu, he died in the army; his princely title was posthumously restored.

units.zh: 安豐王猛，字季烈。
units.en: Meng, Prince of Anfeng, styled Jilie.
units.literal: Prince of Anfeng Meng, style Jilie.

units.zh: 太和五年封，加侍中。
units.en: In Taihe year 5 he received his fief and was made palace attendant.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed and made Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 出為和龍鎮都大將、營州刺史。
units.en: He went out as grand general of Helong garrison and Yingzhou inspector.
units.literal: He was sent out as Grand General of Helong Garrison and Inspector of Ying Province.

units.zh: 猛寬仁雄毅，甚有威略，戎夷畏愛之。
units.en: Meng was broad, benevolent, bold, and resolute, with real martial presence; the frontier peoples both feared and loved him.
units.literal: Meng was broad, benevolent, bold, and resolute, with great martial bearing; the frontier peoples feared and loved him.

units.zh: 薨于州。
units.en: He died in his province.
units.literal: He died in the province.

units.zh: 贈太尉，諡曰匡。
units.en: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant and given the posthumous name Kuang.
units.literal: Posthumously made Grand Commandant; posthumous title Kuang.

units.zh: 子延明，襲。
units.en: His son Yanming succeeded.
units.literal: His son Yanming inherited.

units.zh: 世宗時，授太中大夫。
units.en: Under Shizong he was made grand master of the palace.
units.literal: In Shizong's time he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace.

units.zh: 延昌初，歲大飢，延明乃減家財，以拯賓客數十人，并贍其家。
units.en: Early in Yanchang, in a year of great famine, Yanming spent his household wealth to save several dozen guests and support their families as well.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yanzhang, when the year brought great famine, Yanming then reduced his household wealth to save several dozen guests and also support their families.

units.zh: 至肅宗初，為豫州刺史，甚有政績，累遷給事黃門侍郎。
units.en: At Suzong's accession he became Yuzhou inspector with a strong record of governance and rose to attendant of the yellow gate.
units.literal: By the beginning of Suzong's reign he was made Inspector of Yu Province and had great administrative achievements; he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

units.zh: 延明既博極羣書，兼有文藻，鳩集圖籍萬有餘卷。
units.en: Yanming had read widely and wrote well; he collected more than ten thousand scrolls of maps and books.
units.literal: Yanming had read exhaustively among the books and also possessed literary polish; he gathered more than ten thousand scrolls of maps and writings.

units.zh: 性清儉，不營產業。
units.en: He was by nature frugal and did not amass property.
units.literal: By nature he was pure and frugal and did not pursue estates.

units.zh: 與中山王熙及弟臨淮王彧等，並以才學令望有名於世。
units.en: He, Prince of Zhongshan Xi, and Xi's younger brother Prince of Linhuai Yu were among those whose learning and reputation shone across the age.
units.literal: With the Prince of Zhongshan Xi and his younger brother the Prince of Linhuai Yu and others, all were famed in the world for talent, learning, and commanding esteem.

units.zh: 雖風流造次不及熙、彧，而稽古淳篤過之。
units.en: He lacked Xi and Yu's easy brilliance, but in scholarship and sober depth he outpaced them.
units.literal: Though in graceful ease and ready wit he did not match Xi and Yu, in investigating antiquity and plain earnestness he surpassed them.

units.zh: 尋遷侍中。
units.en: Soon he was made palace attendant.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred to Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 詔與侍中崔光撰定服制。
units.en: He was ordered with Palace Attendant Cui Guang to draft court dress rules.
units.literal: An edict ordered him together with Palace Attendant Cui Guang to compile and fix ritual garb regulations.

units.zh: 後兼尚書右僕射。
units.en: He later served concurrently as right vice director of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: Later he also held the concurrent post of Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 以延明博識多聞，敕監金石事。
units.en: His wide learning earned him charge of epigraphic and bell-cauldron matters.
units.literal: Because Yanming was broadly learned and widely informed, he was commanded to oversee metal and stone inscriptions.

units.zh: 及元法僧反，詔為東道行臺、徐州大都督，節度諸軍事，與都督臨淮王彧、尚書李憲等討法僧。
units.en: When Yuan Faseng rebelled, he was named eastern-route mobile secretariat and grand commander of Xuzhou, with command of all armies, and marched with Prince of Linhuai Yu, Minister Li Xian, and others against Faseng.
units.literal: When Yuan Faseng rebelled, an edict made him Eastern-Route Mobile Secretariat, Grand Commander of Xuzhou, and controller of all military affairs, to campaign against Faseng together with Commander-in-Chief the Prince of Linhuai Yu, Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Xian, and others.

units.zh: 蕭衍遣其豫章王綜鎮徐州。
units.en: Xiao Yan posted his Prince of Yuzhang, Zong, to hold Xuzhou.
units.literal: Xiao Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang Zong to garrison Xuzhou.

units.zh: 延明先牧徐方，甚得民譽，招懷舊土，遠近歸之。
units.en: Having once governed Xu with a strong popular name, he called back the old land and won submission from far and near.
units.literal: Yanming had earlier governed the Xu region and won great praise among the people; he now rallied the old domain, and near and far submitted to him.

units.zh: 綜既降，延明因以軍乘之，復東南之境，至宿豫而還。
units.en: When Zong surrendered, Yanming pressed the pursuit, recovered the southeast as far as Suyu, and withdrew.
units.literal: Once Zong had surrendered, Yanming thereupon drove the army in pursuit, recovered the southeastern territory, and returned on reaching Suyu.

units.zh: 遷都督、徐州刺史。
units.en: He was made commander-in-chief and inspector of Xuzhou.
units.literal: He was transferred to Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 頻經師旅，人物凋弊，延明招攜新故，人悉安業，百姓咸附。
units.en: War had repeatedly ravaged the region; he gathered old and new inhabitants until every household had its livelihood and the people clung to him.
units.literal: The region had repeatedly suffered armies; people and goods were wasted and ruined; Yanming rallied new settlers and old residents alike, so that all settled into their trades and the common folk all attached themselves to him.

units.zh: 莊帝時，兼尚書令、大司馬。
units.en: Under Emperor Zhuang he served concurrently as director of the Masters of Writing and grand marshal.
units.literal: Under Emperor Zhuang he concurrently held Minister of the Masters of Writing and Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 及元顥入洛，延明受顥委寄，率眾守河橋。
units.en: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Yanming was entrusted with his cause and held Heqiao with an army.
units.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yanming received Hao's trust, led troops, and held Heqiao Bridge.

units.zh: 顥敗，遂將妻子奔蕭衍，死於江南。
units.en: Hao's fall sent him south to Xiao Yan with his family; he died in Jiangnan.
units.literal: When Hao was defeated, he took wife and children and fled to Xiao Yan, and died in the lands south of the Yangzi.

units.zh: 莊帝末，喪還。
units.en: Late in Zhuangdi's reign his coffin came home.
units.literal: At the end of Emperor Zhuang's reign his remains were returned.

units.zh: 出帝初，贈太保，王如故，諡曰文宣。
units.en: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne he was posthumously titled grand mentor, his princedom left as before, with the posthumous name Prince Wenzuan.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was posthumously given Grand Mentor, his princedom unchanged, posthumous title Wenzuan.

units.zh: 所著詩賦讚頌銘誄三百餘篇，又撰五經宗略、詩禮別義，注帝王世紀及列仙傳。
units.en: He left more than three hundred poems, fu, hymns, inscriptions, and dirges, compiled Summaries of the Five Classics and Separate Meanings of the Odes and Rites, and annotated the Chronological Record of Emperors and Kings and the Biographies of Transcendents.
units.literal: Works he authored—poems, fu, encomia, hymns, inscriptions, and dirges—numbered more than three hundred pieces; he also compiled Summaries of the Five Classics' Main Points and Separate Meanings of the Odes and Rites, and annotated Huangfu Mi's Chronological Record of Emperors and Kings and the Biographies of Transcendents.

units.zh: 又以河間人信都芳工算術，引之在館。
units.en: He also summoned Xin Du Fang of Hejian, a master of mathematics, to his library.
units.literal: Moreover, because Xin Du Fang of Hejian was skilled in calculation and astronomy, he brought him into his household academy.

units.zh: 其撰古今樂事九章十二圖，又集器準九篇，芳別為之注，皆行於世。
units.en: His nine chapters and twelve diagrams on music through the ages, and nine chapters on instrument measures with Fang's separate commentary, all circulated.
units.literal: He compiled nine chapters and twelve diagrams on music old and new, and also gathered nine chapters on instrument standards; Fang separately annotated them, and all circulated in the world.

units.zh: 論曰：文成五王，安豐特標令望。
units.en: The appraisal says: Among Wencheng's five princes, Anfeng especially stood out with an excellent reputation.
units.literal: The appraisal says: Among Wencheng's five princes, Anfeng especially stood out with an excellent reputation.

units.zh: 延明學業該贍，加以雅談之美；
units.en: Yanming's learning was broad and ample, and he added the refinement of elegant conversation;
units.literal: Yanming's learning was broad and ample, and he added to it the refinement of elegant conversation;

units.zh: 及于永安，運跡冠戎。
units.en: when the Yong'an era came, events placed him at the head of the army.
units.literal: when the Yong'an era came, the course of events placed him at the head of the army.

units.zh: 卒致奔亡，亦其命也。
units.en: That he finally came to flight and exile was also his fate.
units.literal: That he finally came to flight and exile was also his fate.
